title: Official Abaqus time-hardening constant-stress creep case
purpose: Compare AgentFEM's global three-dimensional implicit creep procedure with the material data, held stress, duration, and closed-form response published in the Abaqus creep-integration benchmark.
physics: three-dimensional small-strain Mises time-hardening power-law creep

execution.evidence: The official data use E=20e6 psi, nu=0.3, A=2.5e-27 psi^-5 s^-0.8, n=5, m=-0.2, held stress 20000 psi, and duration 100000 s. The closed-form equivalent creep strain is exactly 0.1. AgentFEM uses 100 uniform backward-Euler increments, so the declared strain tolerance includes the known time-discretization error near t=0.

observables: Mean axial stress over the accepted constitutive quadrature.
Mean committed equivalent creep strain at 100000 seconds.
acceptance: The global finite-element equilibrium retains the prescribed 20000 psi stress.
The committed equivalent creep strain agrees with the official closed-form value 0.1 within the declared backward-Euler discretization tolerance.

quantities.name: mean_axial_stress
quantities.description: Held uniaxial stress from the official input deck.

quantities.name: mean_equivalent_creep_strain
quantities.description: Official closed-form time-hardening creep strain; tolerance covers the versioned 100-step backward-Euler path.

limitations: The official Abaqus specimen is plane stress; AgentFEM uses a homogeneous 3D unit cube with free lateral contraction to reproduce the same uniaxial constitutive state.
The criterion verifies the global Mises creep path against the official closed form, not element-by-element equivalence with CPS4.
This constant-stress case is isothermal and homogeneous even though the current provider also supports MPI, regional materials, Arrhenius temperature fields and portable restart.
